name: Fraud everything theory

card.summary: A looksmaxxing mindset of using any available aid, from lifts to makeup to hair systems, to present the look you want, with confidence, rather than fixing underlying traits.
card.note: A forum philosophy; several of the aids it lists carry their own risks.

quick.overview:
Fraud everything theory is a looksmaxxing framework which holds that the goal is to look a certain way, not to be that way. Its adherents argue for using every cosmetic and presentational aid available, rather than only treatments that change the underlying trait.

The appearance payoff comes from the aids themselves: height insoles for height, skincare and concealer for skin, hair systems for hair, colored contacts for eyes, and confident presentation to tie it together. It is a community philosophy, and no research has tested it as a whole.
quick.how: On the forum thread that describes it, the approach is a list of one aid per perceived flaw, combined with acting as though one effortlessly looks that way.
quick.risks: Some listed items (hormones, injectables, surgery) carry medical risks. One forum reply on the thread reported that using many of these aids left them feeling insecure, while still reporting more success than before.

lead: Fraud everything theory, also called the fraudpill, is a looksmaxxing framework described on looksmax.org. Its premise is that people who avoid concealment methods because they do not fix a root cause can instead embrace them, since society rewards looks and the aim is to look rather than to be [1].

In the originating thread the author lists an aid for each trait: shoe lifts or insoles for height, supplements and training aids for body, filler for bone structure, tretinoin, hydroquinone and concealers for skin, hair systems or micropigmentation for hair, and colored contacts with light makeup for eyes. Age and origin are to be presented by acting the part [1].
Replies in the thread show a mix of responses, including a user who reported that doing most of these left them insecure but with more social success than before [1].

chain: Pick an aid for each perceived flaw
Visible height, skin, hair and eye changes
Confident presentation of the whole look
angle.text: Followers use cosmetic and presentational aids across the body, face and hair and aim to carry the result with confidence.

infobox: Look the part rather than fix the root trait [1]
Shoe lifts, skincare, concealers, hair systems, colored contacts [1]

paras: The thread's author frames the theory as a response to users who decline fillers, implants or surgery because they do not change the underlying bone or cause. The author says the goal is not to be but to look [1].

The idea circulates as a thread rather than an organized movement. Replies range from agreement to a user describing mixed psychological results after using most of the aids, and another reply suggesting working on additional factors [1].

lore.intro: The theory is discussed in a single looksmax.org thread [1].

claims.claim: The goal is to look good, not to be natural
claims.believers: The thread's author says aids for each trait together achieve the look society rewards [1].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined this approach as a whole.
